summary:
The provider qualification harness (SDD#1134, PR #1135) emits a closed fsgg.provider-certification/v1 report from a packed provider artifact, the installed SDD CLI and the installed Governance CLI, and check-report validates it for admission. Review of the first drafts found three reusable failure classes.

Weak oracles where labels stood in for semantics. Required evidence cases named missing, stale and mismatched were only names: a request could give them any non-zero exit and any diagnostic and still pass. Bind each required case to its own behaviour (the Governance diagnostic that defines it and whether evidence was produced) in the request validator, the harness and the report validator. A passing check must carry evidence, and the admission-side validator must check what that evidence says (intended diagnostic, target and staging unchanged, provenance digests equal the report's artifact digests, exit codes), not only that a field is non-empty. Treat a bool as not an int and make the validator total over mistyped evidence: it must return problems, never a traceback.

Overclaim of evidence. The first draft, spec text, docs and roadmap said it proved build, test and package evidence while it exercised exactly one declared capability. State the capability set actually exercised, and say plainly that a report is a producer's self-attestation that check-report cannot authenticate, with tool identities caller-attested.

A skipped or vacuous leg must never certify. Record a leg that cannot run as skipped with a reason and refuse a certified verdict; prove the harness is not vacuous with deliberately bad providers that fail exactly the intended check (and one whose dependants are skipped), and with report tamperings that check-report must detect. Determinism checks must name any excluded volatile field: the provenance records a wall-clock remaining-budget timeoutSeconds, so two identical scaffolds differ by a second (tracked as SDD#1136).
title: Provider certification harness lessons
